title: Smoky Chicken and Rice Bowls with Cheddar-Pepper Sauce
description: The chicken, rice and cheddar from poblano boats become a soft spoonable bowl with a smooth sweet-pepper sauce.
equipment: Small enamel Dutch oven with tight lid, sized to hold the food snugly
Immersion blender and deep heatproof jug

ingredients.name: cooked white rice
ingredients.note: Soft, freshly cooked or promptly chilled.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Use plain broth made from meat, bones and water, with no added vegetable blend or seasonings.

ingredients.name: peeled roasted sweet bell pepper
ingredients.note: Plain, unsalted and seedless; use home-roasted or water-packed without vinegar.

ingredients.name: hot drinking water
ingredients.note: Keep ready; use only as needed to maintain liquid depth or make up the sauce measure.

steps.title: Heat the Traeger
steps.text: Preheat the Traeger Silverton 610 to 300°F with apple and pecan, mixed in equal parts pellets, about 15 minutes with the lid closed.

steps.title: Warm the braising liquid
steps.text: Bring {broth} just to a simmer in the open Dutch oven on the stove, about 3–6 minutes.

steps.title: Smoke the braising liquid
steps.text: Move the uncovered pot to the Traeger grate. Close the smoker lid and smoke the liquid for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Reserve the sauce base
steps.text: Before adding meat, transfer 1 cup of the smoked broth into the HexClad and set aside. Leave the rest in the Dutch oven.

steps.title: Assemble the filling
steps.text: Crumble {chicken} finely into the remaining broth. Fold in {rice}, {garlic} and {cumin}, breaking up clumps. Add {topup} if needed to make a loose, moist mixture.

steps.title: Steam under cover
steps.text: Spread the filling in a shallow, even layer. Fit the lid immediately, with no stall wrap. Cook at 300°F for 20–35 minutes, stirring halfway, until several places in the center register 165°F.

steps.title: Rest the filling
steps.text: Rest covered for 3 minutes so the rice absorbs the juices.

steps.title: Blend the pepper sauce
steps.text: While the filling cooks, blend {pepper} and the reserved clean broth in a deep heatproof jug with an immersion blender until completely smooth. Return the puree to the HexClad.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Bring the skillet liquid to a boil. Whisk in the stirred slurry and simmer for 1 minute, stirring, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Melt the cheddar
steps.text: Take the skillet off the heat and whisk in {cheese} until it melts into the spoon-coating sauce.

steps.title: Serve as soft bowls
steps.text: Fold most of the sauce through the warm rice and chicken. Divide between bowls and spoon the last of the sauce over both tops.

notes: Make ahead: Use freshly cooked rice or cool it promptly in a shallow container and refrigerate. For dairy-free bowls omit cheddar; the thickened pepper puree supplies the sauce. For a mild poblano variation, replace half the sweet pepper with peeled, seeded roasted mild poblano. Refrigerate promptly in shallow portions and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze promptly in small portions with the sauce stirred through; a splash of water restores the rice when reheating. Fridge reheat: Warm one portion covered in its sauce in the HexClad over medium-low heat. Turn gently, adding a splash of water if needed. Check after 6 minutes and continue until the food reaches 165°F throughout. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator. Follow the fridge reheating directions and stir the sauce smooth. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 331 kcal, 28.1 g protein, 22.2 g total carbohydrate, 14.2 g fat, 0.6 g fiber, 177 mg sodium. Includes the measured broth and sauce. Sodium varies with your broth.
